This is a classic presentation of newly diagnosed B-cell precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (BCP-ALL). - 1-week fever and severe nocturnal leg pain → classic symptom of leukemic bone marrow infiltration/inflammation  
- Hb 10.1 g/dL → anemia due to marrow failure  
- WBC 63,000/mm³ with circulating blasts implied by context and marrow findings → leukocytosis driven by malignant lymphoblasts  
- Platelets 27,000/mm³ → profound thrombocytopenia indicating megakaryocyte suppression  
- Bone marrow aspirate shows predominantly immature blasts → morphologic evidence of acute leukemia  
- Flow cytometry: blasts positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT → gold-standard immunophenotypic signature of BCP-ALL  
- No reported expression of myeloid (e.g., MPO, CD13, CD33) or T-cell (e.g., cytoplasmic CD3, CD7) markers → excludes AML and T-ALL  
- Clinical context (age group implied by presentation, absence of lymphadenopathy/mediastinal mass) makes BCP-ALL far more likely than T-ALL or lymphoma

- Karyotype and FISH results — required to assign genetic risk group (e.g., *ETV6-RUNX1* favorable vs *BCR-ABL1* or *KMT2A* adverse)

[DIAGNOSIS]  
B-cell precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (BCP-ALL)
